items.title: Derek Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] You know there’s been so many stories about these kinds of things where people, Al Grey who happened to be a club when the Basie band was there...

ctx.x: He was making, it came out, the album was called “Jazz Piano International.” So he got me and I was representing England, and he got a French pianist by the name of René Urtreger, and we all played like four tracks. And Dick Katz was there who was the American piano player. And that’s how the album came out.

You know there’s been so many stories about these kinds of things where people, Al Grey who happened to be a club when the Basie band was there and their trombone player was sick and the guy said, “get your horn” and he ran, and it’s just little amazing coincidences that helped people.

Well I mean those things work. And I mean that’s, as time goes by, now I’m starting to get a footing, and people say, hey, the kid can play, he speaks kind of weird but he can play, so we’ll hire him. And now, that’s how I got into the studio business. You know what I mean by the studio — playing jingles and record dates and things like that. There was a big band jingle going on, I forget what it was, for what product. But Hank Jones was supposed to be there and for some reason Hank was sick or something and…
